Results show negligible changes in the performance predictions, and baseline validations were then carried out in Modelica. Overall, all data points lie within ±8% of the experimental data. In heating mode, as per ORNL's experimental tests, there was significant heat loss from the cabinet, increasing the deviation between the air-side and refrigerant-side heating capacities. Thus, for the model comparison, the refrigerant-side capacity was used for the heating capacity and COP comparisons, for modeling only. Overall, the models were able to predict baseline HP performance in a laboratory setting and are being used in seasonal simulations to predict the system's overall performance. For the heating mode, all deviations between simulation and Page 65 of 127 DE-EE0009681 University of Maryland, College Park experiment were less than ±8%, with the maximum error of approximately 5% except for the HR1 test case. The high deviation in the HR1 case is due to heat loss through the cabinet, driven by the low (outdoor) air temperature (25°F), leading to a higher simulated (refrigerant) capacity than the measured (airside) capacity. At the same outdoor air temperature, ORNL test data reported airside capacity losses around 10%, and the EPRI test data corroborate this. Note that the current models do not account for cabinet heat losses, and thus, higher deviations are expected as outdoor air temperature continues to decrease.
